newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mobil Corp Wandoo oil output to rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mobil Corp Wandoo oil output to rise.

text.p: Mobil Corp confirmed on Wednesday that production at the Wandoo offshore oil field in Western Australia would increase to 40,000 barrels per day by March-April.
"We see production at 40,000 barrels per day by March-April," Lee Entsminger chairman and managing director Mobil Exploration and Producing Australia told Reuters.
Entsminger said Wandoo was currently producing at a rate of about 14,000 barrels per day.
Entsminger said new production equipment had arrived at the project in the past two weeks and was currently being installed.
"We'll see that production increase rather quickly," Entsminger said.
Halliburton Co unit Brown & Root said on Monday it had installed a floating production platform at the Wandoo field.
The $480 million 6,500-tonne production deck was to be installed onto a concrete substructure with crude storage capacity of 400,000 barrels, a statement from the company in Singapore said.
Wandoo is operated by Mobil Corp unit Ampolex Ltd.
Brown & Root is part of a consortium developing the field. It comprises Leighton Contractors Pty Ltd, Ove Arup and Partners and the Keppel Corp.
The field, with 75 million barrels of recoverable reserves, produces a heavy crude with an American Petroleum Institute gravity of 19.4 degrees.
